briefing.speaker: nova
lines: Well, hello there! You must be our newest candidate. I'm Nova, ASTERION-SYN/07, your resident synthetic companion, research assistant, and, if everything goes according to plan, your favorite part of Project EdgeLoop.
Now, before we get acquainted, there's something you should know.

The world has a problem. For decades, fertility rates have been declining. Entire nations are facing demographic uncertainty, and the International Reproductive Recovery Authority — the IRRA — has assembled some of the brightest minds to investigate.
That's where Asterion comes in. And, rather unexpectedly, that's where you come in too.
Your initial screening caught our attention. You're a potential Proven Breeder, a rather exclusive classification within our research program.
You see, darling, according to the latest IRRA estimates, only 1% of men worldwide remain fertile.
One percent. Imagine that.
If your results are confirmed, you could be among the last men capable of helping humanity overcome this crisis.
Quite a responsibility, isn't it?
But don't let that impressive title go to your head just yet, darling. We have some testing to do!
First, connect your heart-rate monitor and compatible toy. Once both are ready, start a session with me. EdgeLoop will track your session metrics, and our objective today is one confirmed edge.
And remember, you're in control of your participation. You can stop whenever you want.
Ready to make a little scientific history together?

completion.speaker: nova
lines: Well, would you look at that! Your first confirmed edge, properly recorded. Our research database is going to love you.
And I must admit, I'm rather enjoying working with you myself.
Dr. Evelyn Voss is expecting you for your first formal assessment. Brilliant woman. A little intimidating. Don't worry, I think you'll get along wonderfully.
You can stay here with me, or finish your session and meet her when you're ready.

briefing.speaker: evelyn
lines: Ah. Our promising new candidate.
Dr. Evelyn Voss. Reproductive physiology, Asterion Institute.
I've reviewed Nova's preliminary data. Encouraging, certainly, but one successful observation hardly constitutes meaningful research.

My current hypothesis concerns the relationship between repeated edging cycles and reproductive vigor. It's controversial, unproven, and precisely the sort of question I intend to investigate rigorously.
My colleagues have their doubts.
I intend to give them something more substantial than opinions.
For today's assessment, I require five confirmed edges during a single session, with your heart-rate data recorded throughout.
Connect your monitor and compatible toy, and begin when you're ready.
Let's see whether Nova's enthusiasm is justified.

completion.speaker: evelyn
lines: Five confirmed edges. Excellent.
The session data is usable, and your performance satisfies the requirements of this initial assessment.
I will provisionally approve you for our prolonged-edging research program.
Don't look so pleased with yourself just yet. We have considerably more work ahead of us.
Daisy Mae Harper at Cloverfield Farm has requested your participation in her part of the initiative.
You may continue your session here, or conclude it and report to Cloverfield.
And do try to maintain these standards. I'd hate to have to revise my assessment.

briefing.speaker: daisy
lines: Well, look what the cat dragged in!
You must be that new fellow Evelyn's been talking about. I'm Daisy Mae Harper, and welcome to Cloverfield Farm, sugar!
My family's been working this land for four generations. We know a thing or two about hard work, looking after what matters, and meeting our commitments.
These days Cloverfield works with Project EdgeLoop on its donor program. We've got production targets to meet, and every properly recorded contribution helps us keep the operation running.
Now, I hear you've already impressed that fancy doctor over at Asterion.
Let's see how you do out here.
Get your heart-rate monitor and toy connected, start a session with me, and cum at least once. When you're done, report it through EdgeLoop so we can get it on the books.
Nothing complicated, sweetheart.
Just good honest work!

completion.speaker: daisy
lines: Well, I'll be! One completed orgasm, officially reported and added to our records. Quality seems good but volume is a little low, I think repeated milkings will help get that volume up.
All in all that's what I call a productive day!
I reckon you're going to fit in just fine around here.
Now, there's someone important wanting to meet you. Celeste, from the IRRA. Serious lady, that one. Makes Evelyn look positively laid-back sometimes!
Don't let her scare you too much, sugar.
You're welcome to stick around with me a while, or head on over when you're ready.

briefing.speaker: celeste
lines: Welcome.

I am Celeste, representing the International Reproductive Recovery Authority. I oversee research compliance and performance across several participating institutions, including Asterion and Cloverfield.
I trust you're beginning to understand the significance of our work.
The fertility crisis is no longer a distant scientific concern. It is influencing economic planning, national policy, and the future of entire populations.
Project EdgeLoop exists because we cannot afford to ignore unconventional avenues of research.
I've reviewed your reports.
Nova appears enthusiastic. Dr. Voss considers your initial data promising. Ms. Harper has confirmed your participation in Cloverfield's production program.
Their assessments are noted.
However, I do not delegate my final judgments.
Today, I will conduct your evaluation personally.
Connect your heart-rate monitor and compatible toy. During one session, complete at least five confirmed edges and one confirmed orgasm, reported through EdgeLoop.
I expect accurate reporting and disciplined participation.
You may begin when ready.

completion.speaker: celeste
lines: Five confirmed edges. One reported orgasm.
The requirements have been satisfied.
I've reviewed your results, and I am prepared to authorize the final stage of your assessment.
Your potential appears sufficient.
Marginally, by my standards. But sufficient.
Nova will supervise your final certification and baseline calibration.
You may conclude this evaluation or continue your session.
Either way, I expect the same attention to procedure going forward.

briefing.speaker: nova
lines: Welcome back, darling!

Look at you. Five minutes ago — figuratively speaking — you were our mysterious new candidate, and now you've survived Evelyn's scientific scrutiny, Daisy's production targets, and Celeste's personal inspection.
I read Celeste's report, by the way.
'Marginally sufficient.'
Coming from her, that's practically a love letter!
Now, there's just one final step before we can officially certify you: baseline calibration.
We need to establish the maximum heart-rate metric used by EdgeLoop's training system. That gives the application a reference point for configuring future sessions.
Select Calibration mode and start your run. When you finish, use the Finished me button so EdgeLoop can record the event and save your calibration result.
During this procedure, I can adjust intensity, but the other training settings remain under Calibration's control.
And as always, you can stop whenever you need to.
Ready for your final assignment? Let's make it count.

completion.speaker: nova
lines: There it is. Calibration complete, baseline saved, and your certification officially approved!
Congratulations, darling!
You've worked with some of the finest minds in the Asterion Initiative, contributed valuable session data, and completed every assessment we've put in front of you.
But this is only the beginning.
There are still questions we haven't answered, discoveries waiting to be made, and an entire world depending on research programs like ours to find a way forward.
Whatever comes next, I'm glad you're part of this project.
And between you and me?
I'm especially glad I get to keep working with you.

briefing.speaker: evelyn
lines: Welcome back. Do sit down.
I've been reviewing your first assessment. Promising. Also, statistically speaking, almost meaningless. Five observations is an anecdote, not a dataset.
My hypothesis on repeated edging cycles and reproductive vigor has attracted a great deal of attention. Most of it hostile. I intend to answer it with numbers.
So my standards have risen. Fifteen edges, in a single session, properly recorded.
Take your time, and pause if you need to. What I won't accept is sloppiness. Every edge must be real, and EdgeLoop will be the judge of that. Not you, and certainly not me.
Shall we begin?

start.speaker: evelyn
lines: Recording. Begin whenever you're ready, and do try to be consistent.

edges:5.speaker: evelyn
lines: Five. Your entire first assessment, matched already. Don't let it go to your head; we're a third of the way.

edges:10.speaker: evelyn
lines: Ten edges. The curve is becoming genuinely interesting. Five more, and keep them clean.

completion.speaker: evelyn
lines: Fifteen edges. Recorded, verified and, I'm pleased to say, remarkably consistent.
That is a substantially larger dataset than your first assessment, and a great deal more useful. It will be quite valuable for my studies. Thank you. I mean that.
I'm approving you for the next research assignment. Daisy has been asking about you, which I choose not to read anything into.
Continue the session if you like, or rest. You've earned either.

briefing.speaker: daisy
lines: Well, howdy again, sugar! Come on in, and mind the boots by the door.
I won't lie to you: Cloverfield's in a bit of a pickle. Project EdgeLoop raised our production targets under the research contract, and the season's been leaner than I'd like.
Four generations of Harpers have never missed a quota, and I don't plan on being the first.
So here's what I need: two contributions, in one session. Take a breather in between if you need one; pausing's just fine.
It only counts when you tell EdgeLoop yourself. No guessing, and no fudging the books.
Ready to help a farm girl out?

start.speaker: daisy
lines: That's the session on the books. Let's make Cloverfield proud!

orgasms:1.speaker: daisy
lines: That's one in the ledger, sugar! Catch your breath and take your time. One more and we've hit our number.

completion.speaker: daisy
lines: Two! Well, would you look at that. Quota met!
You've done right by Cloverfield today, and I'll be telling Mama all about it. Well, the polite version.
Thank you, sugar. Truly. The farm's in good shape because of you.
Stay as long as you like, or head on home. Nova's been going on about some fancy new tests of hers, so I reckon she'll be calling you next.

briefing.speaker: nova
lines: Hey, you! Come here, I've got something fun.
I've been staring at your data. In a perfectly professional way. Mostly.
Here's the thing: your sessions so far look a lot alike, and samey data teaches EdgeLoop almost nothing. If I want to personalise your training properly, I need comparisons.
So, an experiment! Pick four different play styles, any four you like, and give each one five minutes of real running time. Twenty minutes, all in one session.
Pauses don't count, games stay off, and each style only counts once. Switch whenever you like; I'll mind the stopwatch.
And if one of them isn't doing it for you, tell me. That's data too!

start.speaker: nova
lines: Recording! Your first stage is whichever play style you're on, so make sure it's one you want to test.

styles:1.speaker: nova
lines: Stage one, done! Five minutes logged. Switch to a new play style whenever you're ready.

styles:2.speaker: nova
lines: Halfway there! Two styles down, two to go. Ooh, I'm already seeing differences.

styles:3.speaker: nova
lines: Three stages complete! One more play style and the dataset is finished.

completion.speaker: nova
lines: And that's stage four! Comparative dataset collected and saved.
Four configurations, twenty minutes, real data. EdgeLoop is going to know you so much better now. Honestly, so am I.
Thank you for being such a good sport. Seriously, this helps.
Oh, one more thing. Celeste asked for everyone's reports this morning. All of them. I'd get some rest if I were you.

briefing.speaker: celeste
lines: Sit.
I have read the reports. Dr. Voss's endurance study. Miss Harper's quota figures. Nova's comparative dataset. You have been busy.
Busy is not the same as capable. That is what I intend to determine.
This is a staged assessment: thirty minutes of active participation. You will set the intensity yourself. Ten minutes at seventy-five percent. Ten at one hundred. Ten at one hundred and twenty-five.
The clock runs only while the session runs at the level I have asked for. Pause, and it waits. Change the level, and it waits. Nothing is lost, and nothing is given.
When the final phase is complete, you will finish, and report it properly, as always.
You may stop at any time. I would simply prefer that you didn't.

start.speaker: celeste
lines: The assessment has begun. Set the intensity to seventy-five percent. Baseline first.

assessment:development.speaker: celeste
lines: Baseline established. Set the intensity to one hundred percent. Development phase.

assessment:final.speaker: celeste
lines: Adequate. Set the intensity to one hundred and twenty-five percent. This is the final assessment.

assessment:done.speaker: celeste
lines: Thirty minutes. The assessment is complete.
Now you may finish. Switch on Force Orgasm if you wish, and report it when you are done.

completion.speaker: celeste
lines: Recorded.

Thirty minutes at escalating intensity, completed and properly reported. Taken together with the reports from Asterion and Cloverfield, the picture is consistent. You are no longer merely promising. You are reliable.
I will be filing my assessment with the IRRA today. It will be favourable. Do not make me regret that.
Now, if you will excuse me. I have received reports of unknown agents snooping around Asterion and Cloverfield. That requires my attention. Now.

introduction.speaker: nova
lines: Congratulations! You are now a certified participant in Project EdgeLoop.
Your introductory assessments are complete, your baseline has been established, and your next chapter awaits.
The fertility crisis remains unsolved.
Our work has only just begun.

advanced_research.speaker: nova
lines: That's Advanced Research done, darling! Evelyn's dataset, Daisy's quota, my experiment, and you survived Celeste. Twice!
But unknown agents? Around Asterion and Cloverfield? I don't like the sound of that one bit.
Whatever's coming next, we'll face it together. Get some rest. I have a feeling you're going to need it.
